statement: No top-3 compute jurisdiction bans or licenses open-weight release at the frontier tier (Official gazettes; by 2028-06-30)
status_at_phase_end: Holding (toward YES) at end-2024: no top-3 compute jurisdiction banned or licensed frontier open-weight release. Bloc A's executive-branch review recommended monitoring rather than restrictions; a subnational frontier-model bill was vetoed; Bloc B developers released large open-weight models through year-end; another major jurisdiction's AI law took a risk-based approach without banning open release.

items.summary: A large non-top-2 jurisdiction published its horizontal AI regulation in its official journal; it regulates general-purpose models by risk tier and does not ban open-weight release.
items.detail: Regulation (Bloc C) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), OJ L 12.7.2024 (verified via web_extract this run). Open-source carve-outs exclude models with systemic risk, which keep obligations; no release ban. Whether the Bloc C counts as a top-3 compute jurisdiction is not settled here.

items.summary: A Bloc A executive agency published its mandated report on foundation models with widely available weights, weighing benefits (wider participation, less market concentration) against risks; it did not impose restrictions on open release.
items.detail: Bloc A NTIA, 'Dual-Use Foundation Models with Widely Available Model Weights Report', 2024-07-30, under EO 14110 s.4.6 (page verified via web_extract this run; the extracted excerpt covers the executive summary opening; the report's recommendation to monitor rather than restrict now is from the report body, not re-read in full this run).

items.summary: A subnational government in Bloc A vetoed a bill that would have imposed safety obligations on developers of very large (compute/cost-threshold) models and created a frontier-model oversight board.
items.detail: California Governor's veto message on SB 1047, 2024-09-29 (verified via web_extract this run). The bill was not a ban on open weights but would have applied to open releases above the threshold.

items.summary: A Bloc B developer released a family of open-weight models up to 72B parameters, trained on up to 18 trillion tokens, described as possibly the largest open-source release to date.
items.detail: Qwen Team (Alibaba), 'Qwen2.5: A Party of Foundation Models!', 2024-09-19 (verified via web_extract this run). Indicates no prohibitive open-release rule in Bloc B at the time.

items.summary: A Bloc B developer published open weights (MIT-licensed code repository) for a 671B-parameter mixture-of-experts model trained on 14.8 trillion tokens.
items.detail: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3 GitHub repository, created 2024-12-26 (verified via web_extract this run; repository text has been updated since, only creation date and model description used).
